method: Ran each page in Playwright at 1280x900 and 400x850, captured first frame, settled hero and a full scroll, opened the mobile menu and pressed Escape, tabbed to check focus rings, and measured horizontal overflow and tiny text. Compared legibility over animation, overlaps and first-frame state across all four.

matter.best: Footer wordmark and the heat-ramp palette are striking, and focus rings are visible (dashed 2px).
matter.worst: The molten stream runs straight through the hero copy: on desktop it clips the end of the h1 ('it'), and at 400px it overprints the eyebrow ('SETTLES'), the paragraph and the hint text, which is also drawn over the pool.
matter.evidence: No horizontal overflow at 400px and no console errors. Hero stream collides with headline and body at both widths. Nav logo is a faint tiny mark at 400px. Button labels inside the canvas buttons are about 9px. Desktop sections have large dead gaps, and the Pour canvas sits oddly offset from its copy. Mobile menu overlay is translucent over the hero.

signal.best: Most consistent component system: spec cards, tabs and rule strip are tidy, type hierarchy is clean, and the amber focus ring on nav links is clear.
signal.worst: The first still frame is awkward: the wordmark is half-formed and clipped with a huge empty band before the headline, and at 400px the hero has large blank stretches. The mobile menu overlay lets ghosted hero text bleed behind the links.
signal.evidence: Settled desktop hero is strong, but at 300ms the wordmark is cut mid-height. The nav mark is smeared at small size. Some 9px text ('v' in the dropdown caret). No overflow at 400px, no errors, Escape closes the menu. Hint text under the CTA is dim grey on dark, low contrast.

sky.best: Most shippable: text sits in solid translucent panels over the animation so every line stays legible, the type hierarchy is clear, and the mobile layout is clean with stacked CTAs and an opaque full-screen menu.
sky.worst: The fixed time-of-day HUD pill covers content at the bottom of the viewport, 10px labels on the buttons are small, and the hero wordmark is absent in the first frame (it forms later).
sky.evidence: At 400px nothing overlaps or clips, and the burger turns into a close button. Focus ring is a 2px outline plus a 5px glow, the best of the four. Escape closes the menu. No errors. The boxed paragraphs give the hero a slightly heavy look, and the first still frame shows the hero copy before the logo.

creatures.best: Polished type and layout: a bold display face, a clean hero with a good first frame, tidy button cards at 400px, and a solid-bordered mobile menu panel.
creatures.worst: The hint paragraph is drawn over fish and flora and is hard to read. The 400px eyebrow wraps with tight leading. The nav wordmark is clipped and smeared at the top at 400px. Section headings show through the translucent nav. The wordmark demo canvas looks nearly empty on scroll.
creatures.evidence: No overflow, no errors. Hero reads well at desktop. At 400px 'Watch the dive' is overprinted by jellyfish art. The mobile menu panel lets hero buttons show beneath it. Focus ring is a solid 2px gold pill, visible. Sections are tightly spaced, with a good dusk footer scene and clear link columns.

one_line_verdict: Sky is the only one that reads like a finished product: legible panels over the animation, a clean 400px layout and a solid mobile menu, while the others have text colliding with the animation or awkward first frames.
